🐰 Medical Students

Welcome to the clinic essentials page! This is meant to be a calm, practical guide for how our clinic runs and what you should do each visit.

💗 **Goal:** Help you feel prepared, confident, and supported in clinic—without information overload.

✨ Quick Start

  • 👉 Check the schedule Look for Dr. Morgan
    • Search: MOB NEUR
      • (If on the 4th Floor, hover over the name and click on the schedule that says 4th floor)
      • (If on the 2nd Floor, hover over the name and click on the schedule that says 2nd floor)
      • (If not able to find a patient click the schedule that says MOB NEURO GME MA)
  • 🧠 Only prior “must-know”: how to administer a MoCA
  • 📄 New patient? Give the clinic info sheet (first file folder in the yellow/blue binder)

👯 People to Know

  • Caty — Scribe
  • Erica — Social Worker
  • Deva — Fellow

🗺️ How Clinic Works (the flow)

  • We typically see one patient at a time → you present to the physician → then move to the next patient.
  • We see Memory (AD) and Movement (PD) disorders (check schedule/referral).
  • You write the note for the patient you see.
  • Notes are due within 3 days of starting them.
  • If a patient is established we look at the prior note to see if there were
    • (A) Plans scheduled for clinic
    • (B) Any referrals, orders, or medications you should cover/ask questions about
  • If a patient is new:
    • Look for “refer” for a referral in the top search bar to determine why there are here today
  • If you’re unsure about anything, ask — we’re all here to help 🐰🤍

🧠 Cognitive Tests: MoCA

  • MoCA is typically done yearly
  • If a pt is on infusions, its done every 5-6 months
  • You can skip if: 1) medical concerns make it an unfair assessment, or 2) patient is < 12/30
  • MoCAs are in the first folder in the pink binder (v7.1) — ask us to print more if needed
  • If patient remembers the MoCA, use the alternate version v7.2

🌸 Question Guide (use for your HPI)

💗 **Important:** **All patients should be asked the bolded items + all mood questions.**
  • Memory patients: Cognitive + Mood + Bolded items
  • Motor patients: Motor + Mood + Bolded items

📝 Before you enter the room

  • Review the last note / referral (why are they here today?)
  • Review meds with the patient in the room (keep chart up to date)

🐰 HPI Sections (copy this structure)

💊 Current Medications

  • Any med related to treatment, memory, or motor
  • If receiving infusions: confirm which infusion number
    • Find more infusion information for clinic here

🧪 Trialed Medications

  • What was tried + why it was stopped (side effects, inefficacy, etc.)

🧠 Cognitive

  • Memory trouble (onset, progression, recent changes):
  • Awareness of deficits:
  • Repetition / names / losing items:
  • ADLs: bathing, dressing, toileting, brushing teeth, feeding
  • IADLs: driving, cooking, finances, meds, call/text ability
  • Hallucinations/delusions (description & timing):
  • Cognitive therapy:
  • Wandering:
  • Sundowning:

🚶 Motor

  • Hearing changes:
  • Rigidity:
  • Tremors:
  • Freezing of gait:
  • Dyskinesia:
  • Falls (frequency, near-falls, catching self):
  • Balance/gait issues:
  • Exercise habits:
  • Swallowing/choking/sialorrhea:
  • Constipation/incontinence:
  • Lightheadedness/dizziness:

💗 Mood / Sleep / Behavior

  • Speech/language changes:
  • Mood/personality:
  • Aggression/irritability:
  • Sleep quality/changes:
  • Impulse control issues (DA meds):
  • Appetite:

🧺 “Other” (anything not captured above)

  • Anything discussed that doesn’t neatly fit the categories

🧬 Family History

  • Stroke, thyroid, TBI, sleep apnea, alcohol, anemia, dementia, Parkinson’s, tremor, RLS, other

🏡 Social History

  • Location:
  • Education:
  • Occupation:
  • Retirement:
  • Habits:

🩺 In the room (what to actually do)

  • Use the question guide + clinical skills you’ve learned.
  • If you want to do a physical exam, only do what’s safe (we want zero falls—use your judgment).

🗣️ Presenting to the preceptor

🐾 No need to overthink—clear and structured is best.

📝 Notes & Format (EPIC)

🧾 Starting the note

  • Create Note → choose Standard Visit Note

🪪 Patient ID (2 sentences)

  • Sentence 1: name, age, new/returning, problem (AD/PD), relevant PMHx, visit type (f/u/referral/results)
  • Sentence 2: who is accompanying them
  • Include pt current medications and trialed medications related to memory or movement medication
    • You can usually copy this from the last note

✍️ HPI

  • Meds should be in a header/bullet format:
    • Current meds: name + # tablets + time of day
    • Trialed meds: name + reason stopped
  • Paragraph form of questions asked
  • Tests/labs/imaging reviewed: include header with date + paste impression/results OR/AND copy over from last note

🧠 ROS / PE

  • May copy from prior note or use smartphrases + edit for both ROS and PE
  • MoCA + gait often edited in PE:
    • include date
    • include total score
    • include delayed recall score

🧩 Assessment (how we structure it)

  • Copy Patient ID
  • 1–2 sentences: chief complaints from HPI
  • If MoCA done: include score (if not, skip)
  • Brief exam changes or stable findings
  • Brief test/lab/imaging results reviewed
  • Then: “Today we plan to ____.”
  • End with: “Pt will RTC in __ months for f/u for ____.”

✍️ Scribe lines

Put the dot phrase .celmedstudent at the bottom of the note to sign that this is your note

🎀 You’re done! How to send the note 😗

✅ Problem List (THIS VISIT tab)

Go to Problem List → in Current A&P only, include:

  • Rx (dose)
  • Order (tests/labs/scans)
  • Referral (HH PT/OT/ST/program/provider)
  • Information given
  • Monitor (what to track)
  • Continue current medications
  • Continue physical & mental exercise
  • RTC in # months

Then click Accept

📅 Follow-up

  • Scroll to Follow Up → select return timeframe
  • Send note to John C Morgan to sign
